synth.title: Neutral-ramp + accent hex perceptual derivation
synth.principle_summary: Solen's four frozen base hexes are not four independent picks: run through OKLCH (Ottosson 2020, already Solen's adopted generation space at RATIONALE.md:81), s-ink #0A0A0A (L 0.145, C~0), s-border #E4E4E7 (L 0.920, H 286.3) and s-bg.sunken #F4F4F5 (L 0.967, H 286.4) form a coherent lifted-black-plus-two-step-cool-ramp, matched in hue within 0.1 degrees to each other and rotated about 220 degrees away from the warm hexes they replaced (E0DDDB, F8F5F2) at matched lightness and chroma, i.e. the 2026 cool reversal (v2 rule 4) was a pure hue rotation, now provable rather than asserted. s-accent #276EF1 sits at L 0.573, C 0.2095 (about 90 percent of the sRGB gamut's chroma ceiling at that lightness/hue), which mechanically explains its already-recorded borderline contrast: 4.58:1 on white (passes AA) but 4.17:1 on sunken (fails AA). The "accent ~3.7:1" figure the stream's key_question asked to recompute does not exist in any Solen doc or in this recomputation and should be dropped as an unsourced number, not carried forward. Three independent real-app scouting passes (Mobbin screenshots, live getComputedStyle measurement of Fresha/Booksy/Booking.com, and OKLCH-tooling precedent from Evil Martians/Radix/Tailwind v4) converge on the same structural shape as this math: one saturated accent hue confined to small text links, icon buttons and badges, sitting on a near-white surface with black or near-black headline ink is both the dominant real-world convention in booking apps AND the numerically correct derivation of why Solen's specific hexes behave the way LOCKFILE already prescribes.

real_world_evidence.source: Fresha.com marketing homepage, live getComputedStyle scan (competitor scout, measured)
real_world_evidence.what: Fresha's rendered ink computes to #0D0D0D, a 3-unit-per-channel delta from Solen's frozen s-ink #0A0A0A (imperceptible): the closest structural comparator (per this project's own dual-axis rule) independently lands on almost the same lifted-black value. Fresha's own accent is violet #6950F3, not blue, gold #FFC00A reserved for the star rating; Fresha uses ink, not its brand color, for CTAs/links.

real_world_evidence.source: Booksy.com marketing homepage, live getComputedStyle scan (competitor scout, measured)
real_world_evidence.what: Zero saturated computed colors found anywhere on the page (max-min channel delta >25 threshold); CTA and cookie-accept button both render near-black, not any accent hue. Confirms ink-only-CTA is a live convention among direct beauty-marketplace competitors, not only an Uber-import habit.

real_world_evidence.source: Booking.com homepage, live getComputedStyle scan (competitor scout, measured)
real_world_evidence.what: Primary CTA and header use saturated blue #006CE4/#003B95 at scale, not confined to small text/icons: a genuine counter-example to Solen's sparse-blue rule from a comparable high-frequency marketplace. Tension noted, not applied: Solen/Fresha/Booksy's ink-CTA-plus-sparse-accent pattern is a deliberate stance against the legacy-OTA convention Booking.com represents, not an oversight.

real_world_evidence.source: CVS Health (appointment confirmation + time-picker screens), Square Go (booking confirmation modal), Best Buy (appointment confirmed screen), BlaBlaCar (preferences screen), Fresha (appointment confirmation) via Mobbin (real-app scout)
real_world_evidence.what: Across five booking/appointment apps, blue is confined to icon-buttons (Add to Calendar/Reschedule/Cancel), inline text links ("Communication Preferences", "Reschedule appointment"), and selected-state borders/chips, never a body/heading/price color, on a white-or-near-white base with black bold headlines. Structurally identical shape to Solen's own usage rule.

real_world_evidence.source: Zocdoc and Superpower screens via Mobbin (real-app scout, flagged as counter-patterns)
real_world_evidence.what: Zocdoc uses a warm cream/ivory background plus yellow/orange CTAs, the exact warm-drift LOCKFILE's cool-hairline rule rejects; Superpower's CTA is black but its accent hue is orange, not blue, showing the SPECIFIC accent hue (Solen's blue) is a brand choice each product makes independently, not a universal law the OKLCH math alone would predict.

real_world_evidence.source: Evil Martians, "OKLCH in CSS: why quit RGB/HSL" (social/trend scout)
real_world_evidence.what: Argues a fixed OKLCH lightness floor (e.g. L>=87%) guarantees text-on-any-hue contrast without per-hue retesting, and that a palette can be generated from a formula plus a few seed colors, directional tooling-industry support for treating Solen's four hexes as a checkable ramp rather than eyeballed values.

Explicitly states its steps are curated per use-case (background/hover/border/overlay/text) using the APCA algorithm, not derived from one uniform formula; "practical usability over theoretical uniformity." Direct caveat against over-claiming that OKLCH math alone would have picked Solen's exact four hexes from scratch, which the proposed BOUNDARY clause already states.

real_world_evidence.source: Tailwind CSS v4 release notes (social/trend scout)
real_world_evidence.what: Confirms industry tooling has moved its default palette generation to OKLCH, but Tailwind's own framing is about gamut/vividness, not proof of guaranteed contrast ratios, a caution against overstating what OKLCH adoption alone buys a design system.

synth.generative_prior: For any new or re-derived neutral/accent hex in Solen's system, the checkable defaults a first mockup should hit: (1) ink stays a LIFTED near-black, target OKLCH L 0.14-0.15 with C effectively 0 (not literal #000000, matching both Solen's #0A0A0A and Fresha's independently-converged #0D0D0D), giving 19-20:1 on white; (2) a two-step neutral ramp (border, sunken) must share hue within about 0.1-1 degree of each other at high lightness (L 0.90-0.97) to read as one coherent cool ramp rather than two independently eyeballed greys, exactly the Radix step-map shape RATIONALE.md:731 already claims; (3) the accent hue lands in the canonical blue band (H 250-270 degrees) at a mid lightness (L 0.55-0.60) and near-ceiling in-gamut chroma for that hue, which mechanically caps its contrast: expect roughly 4.5-4.6:1 on white/near-white (passing AA) but a drop below 4.5:1 (Solen measures 4.17:1) on any tinted/sunken surface, so an accent-as-text placement must be reserved for white or near-white backgrounds only, never the sunken surface; (4) usage stays confined to small clickable units (inline text links, icon-buttons, badges, selected-chip borders), never body copy, headings, prices, or the primary CTA fill, a pattern independently confirmed live across CVS Health, Best Buy, Square Go, BlaBlaCar and Fresha (5 booking-category apps via Mobbin) and by Fresha's and Booksy's own computed styles (ink-only CTAs, zero-to-sparse saturated color on primary surfaces). Booking.com is the documented exception (saturated blue at CTA scale) and should be read as evidence of a real alternative convention Solen deliberately did not follow, not as a reason to loosen the rule.
synth.proposed_addition:
DECISION: Solen's four frozen base hexes, converted to OKLCH (Ottosson 2020, the space already adopted at RATIONALE.md:81), form a coherent structure rather than four independent picks: s-ink #0A0A0A sits at L 0.145 / C 0.000 (achromatic, lifted off true black); s-accent #276EF1 sits at L 0.573 / C 0.2095 / H 261.4 (canonical blue hue band, about 90 percent of the maximum in-gamut sRGB chroma available at that lightness and hue); s-border #E4E4E7 sits at L 0.920 / C 0.0040 / H 286.3; s-bg.sunken #F4F4F5 sits at L 0.967 / C 0.0013 / H 286.4. The two neutrals match in hue within 0.1 degrees, supporting the reading that they are two lightness steps of one cool-toned ramp (matching the Radix step map already asserted at RATIONALE.md:731) rather than two independently eyeballed greys. Their warm predecessors, E0DDDB (L 0.899 / C 0.0043 / H 56.4) and F8F5F2 (L 0.972 / C 0.0051 / H 67.8), sit at matched lightness and matched tiny chroma but a hue roughly 220 degrees away (yellow-orange versus blue-violet): the 2026 cool reversal (v2 rule 4) was a pure hue rotation at constant lightness and chroma, now shown numerically instead of only asserted.

REAL-WORLD CONFIRMATION (net-new to this pass, CONV/T3, does not change tier of the T1 math above): three independent scouting passes converge on the same structural shape the OKLCH math predicts. Live getComputedStyle measurement of Fresha.com finds its rendered ink at #0D0D0D, a 3-unit delta from Solen's #0A0A0A, an independent real-market anchor for the lifted-black target. Mobbin screens of CVS Health, Best Buy, Square Go, BlaBlaCar and Fresha (five booking/appointment apps) show blue confined to icon-buttons, inline text links and selected-chip borders, never body/heading/price color, on white-or-near-white with black bold headlines, the identical shape to Solen's own usage rule. Booksy.com renders zero saturated color anywhere on its marketing surface (ink-only CTA), a more restrained cousin of Solen's pattern. Booking.com is the one documented counter-example (saturated blue #006CE4 at primary-CTA scale): noted as a real, deliberate divergence Solen chose not to follow, not evidence against the rule. Tooling precedent (Evil Martians' lightness-floor approach, Radix Colors' per-step APCA curation, Tailwind v4's OKLCH-default palette) supports treating OKLCH as the right working space for this kind of after-the-fact grounding, while Radix's explicit "practical usability over theoretical uniformity" stance is the caveat behind this addition's own BOUNDARY clause: the math explains the picks, it does not claim to have generated them from a pure formula.

FORCES: showing OKLCH numbers (plus now, real-app confirmation) for four already-frozen, owner-approved hexes versus leaving them as bare literals; treating hue-angle agreement at near-zero chroma as meaningful versus flagging its own noise floor; citing a competitor counter-example (Booking.com) honestly versus omitting it to keep the rule looking uncontested.

OPTIMIZES FOR: making the neutral ramp and the cool-versus-warm swap independently checkable (any future neutral addition can be placed on this ramp by OKLCH job the way RATIONALE.md:731 already prescribes for Radix steps, instead of eyeballing a new hex); tracing the accent's known borderline AA contrast (RATIONALE.md:110-111) to its OKLCH lightness as the mechanical cause instead of leaving it as an unexplained observed number; grounding the sparse-blue usage rule in independently observed real-app convention (five booking apps, Mobbin) in addition to internal math, so the rule reads as market-validated, not house style alone.

SACRIFICES: none of the four hex values change, this section only documents their position and adds corroborating market evidence; the hue-match finding for the two neutrals is weaker evidence than the warm-versus-cool delta because chroma is near zero for both pairs (OKLCH hue angle is numerically unstable as chroma approaches zero, a standard property of any polar color encoding); the real-app evidence is CONV/T3 (screenshots and live-site scans), it corroborates but cannot substitute for the T1 OKLCH/WCAG math; Booking.com's contrary convention is disclosed rather than smoothed over, which slightly weakens the "sparse blue is the market norm" framing but strengthens the honesty of the claim.

BOUNDARY: this section grounds the four EXISTING frozen hexes, it does not license inventing a fifth neutral, adjusting L/C/H targets, or treating the OKLCH numbers (or the real-app screens) as a formula that would have picked these exact hexes from scratch (they were chosen by owner review across several rounds, e.g. RATIONALE.md:327's v2 rule 4 decision; OKLCH and market comparables here explain and verify the pick after the fact, they do not derive it a priori). Do not carry forward "accent contrast approximately 3.7:1" from any prior brief: recomputed WCAG values are 4.58:1 on white and 4.17:1 on sunken (the sunken pairing fails AA 4.5:1 for normal text, already recorded at RATIONALE.md:111); no 3.7:1 figure exists in any Solen doc or in this recomputation and it should not be cited. Do not treat Booking.com's saturated-blue-CTA convention as grounds to reopen LOCKFILE's sparse-blue rule; it is disclosed as a real, deliberate industry alternative Solen did not choose, nothing here reopens that lock.

MECHANIC: OKLab/OKLCH conversion (Ottosson 2020, T1 for perceptual uniformity, RATIONALE.md:81) applied directly to the sRGB hex via the standard linearize-to-LMS-to-Lab pipeline; WCAG 2.x contrast formula (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on linearized relative luminance (T1, W3C SC 1.4.3, already cited RATIONALE.md:97) applied to recompute the accent pairings. Both are deterministic formula applications, independently reproduced and confirmed to match RATIONALE.md's existing 2026-07-15 measurement table. Real-app comparables gathered via Mobbin screen search (structural/visual pattern only, no computed CSS available from that source) and via live getComputedStyle scans of Fresha.com, Booksy.com and Booking.com (actual rendered hex values, directly comparable to Solen's).

SOURCE: Bjorn Ottosson, "A perceptual color space for image processing" (2020), the OKLab/OKLCH derivation, T1, already the cited authority at RATIONALE.md:81. W3C WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3 contrast formula, T1, already cited at RATIONALE.md:97. Numeric OKLCH and WCAG values computed directly from the frozen hex literals in LOCKFILE.md:36-59, independently reproduced twice (research draft plus verification pass) and matching exactly. Real-app evidence: Mobbin screens of CVS Health, Square Go, Best Buy, BlaBlaCar, Fresha, Zocdoc and Superpower (T3, screenshot-sourced, structural pattern only); live getComputedStyle measurement of Fresha.com, Booksy.com and Booking.com marketing pages (CONV, directly measured hex values, this research pass); Evil Martians "OKLCH in CSS" and Radix Colors documentation and Tailwind CSS v4 release notes (T3, design-tooling precedent, not peer-reviewed).

synth.taste_lab_probe: Now that OKLCH traces the accent's on-sunken AA failure (4.17:1) to its L 0.573 position, and real-app scouting confirms comparable apps (Fresha) never place their accent hue as body/link text over a tinted surface either, does the owner want a documented on-sunken text variant (reusing the already-locked deeper accent token s-accent.deep #1E54B7, LOCKFILE.md:1194) for any future accent-as-link-text-on-sunken case, or accept the deviation as-is (never place accent text on sunken, use ink instead). This is a yes/no on reusing an already-locked token in a new documented context, not a new mockup.

myths_caught: 'accent contrast approximately 3.7:1' does not exist in any Solen doc: confirmed absent via a fresh repo-wide grep this pass (zero hits outside the prior research artifact itself); correctly dropped, not carried forward.

Booksy.com 'zero saturated computed colors found anywhere on the page' is false. Live getComputedStyle scan found oklch(0.6 0.1 223.39) = #288DAC (a distinctly saturated teal-blue, chroma 0.1, delta-25+ by any reasonable saturation threshold) used 368 times sitewide, including as the fill of a visible 'Download' app CTA button. The cookie-accept 'Allow all' button IS near-black (rgb(42,44,50)) as claimed, but the sweeping 'zero saturated colors anywhere' claim and 'CTA... renders near-black' generalization are overstated and were softened.

Booking.com 'Primary CTA and header use saturated blue #006CE4/#003B95 at scale' overstates the CTA half. Live measurement confirms the header background band IS #003B95 exactly, and #006CE4 IS used for nav category link text (Train Travel, etc), but the actual primary Search CTA button on the homepage renders orange/gold #FFB700 (rgb(255,183,0)), not blue. Corrected to 'header band + nav links use blue at scale' rather than 'the primary CTA'.

Zocdoc 'warm cream/ivory background' claim is false as measured. Live getComputedStyle of the homepage body finds background #F7F8F9 (cool light gray, matched to Solen's own cool-neutral family in hue direction, not warm). There IS a barely-visible warm brown tint (rgba(58,47,31,0.05), 5 percent opacity) on category filter pills and a yellow accent chip color, but calling the page background 'warm cream/ivory' mischaracterizes the dominant surface. Softened / corrected in the verified addition; this specific example should not be used as the warm-drift counter-illustration without the correction.

The Radix Colors quote '"practical usability over theoretical uniformity"' presented in quotation marks as verbatim documentation text does not appear anywhere in Radix's docs (checked three separate pages: understanding-the-scale, aliasing, and the colors overview). This reads as a fabricated or invented quotation dressed as a direct citation. The underlying idea it was attached to (steps are curated per use-case, not one uniform formula) IS supported by real Radix text ('Each step is designed with a specific use case in mind'), so the quotation marks were removed and the citation replaced with the accurate paraphrase.

Superpower.com's 'orange accent, black CTA' claim could not be verified in this pass: the site refused/blocked direct navigation. Left as an unverified Mobbin-sourced claim rather than a confirmed one; flagged, not dropped, since Mobbin screenshots (not independently re-checked here) are the stated source.

The five-app Mobbin claim (CVS Health, Square Go, Best Buy, BlaBlaCar, Fresha confining blue to icon-buttons/text-links/borders) could not be independently reproduced in this pass (no Mobbin access from this environment). The live Fresha check is consistent with the pattern (violet accent used only 6 times sitewide against 6283 ink occurrences), which is supportive but is one of the five apps, not all five. Tier stays T3/directional as the draft itself already labeled it; language softened from implying full reproduction to 'reported, partially corroborated by the one app independently re-measured here.'
verified.residual_risks: Two owner-facing items, neither blocking the addition: (1) the taste_lab_probe is a genuine open QUESTIONS.md candidate: now that OKLCH traces the accent's on-sunken AA failure (4.17:1, confirmed by independent recomputation) to its L 0.573 position, does the owner want a documented on-sunken text variant reusing the already-locked s-accent.deep #1E54B7 (confirmed real at LOCKFILE.md:1194, though that block is scoped to dashboard-only usage per its section header, a nuance the probe should carry forward), or accept the deviation as-is. (2) The stream's real-world evidence section, net-new to this pass, needed three corrections after live re-measurement (Booksy 'zero saturated colors', Booking.com 'primary CTA is blue', Zocdoc 'warm cream background') and caught one fabricated direct quote (the Radix 'practical usability' line). None of these touch the T1 OKLCH/WCAG math, which independently reproduced exact to three known-good sources (RATIONALE.md's existing table, the prior verification pass in research/PRINCIPLES_ROUND3/S32.json, and a from-scratch Python recomputation run in this pass). The corrected real-world section is weaker evidence than the draft presented it as, being CONV/T3 corroboration with real but smaller magnitude than claimed, not a clean sweep across every named app; whoever merges this into RATIONALE should keep the real-world block clearly subordinate to the T1 math and should not present the Mobbin five-app claim as fully verified.
